title: Fourier concentration from decision trees
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $A$ be a set of available coordinates among $n$ coordinates, and let $T$ be a decision tree on $A$ with real outputs. Suppose that $f$ maps the binary cube on $n$ coordinates to $ br$, that $T$ computes $f$, and that $f$ takes only the values $-1$ and $1$. For $0<\varepsilon\le 1$, the sum of the squared Fourier coefficients of the corresponding function on the sign cube, over all coordinate sets $S$ whose size exceeds $\left\lceil\log_2\!\left(\frac{\mathrm{leafCount}(T)}{\varepsilon}\right)\right\rceil$, is at most $\varepsilon$.
